title: In this world, every promise grows a flower out of your skin.
formula: Rule as the hook (every promise grows a flower out of your skin; kept = bloom, broken = rot + stink) -> world tour (Linda's marathon sunflower, Dad's six-year sink tulip, the 'I'll call you' guy you smell across the mall) -> rival's perfect version (Derek: 1,000 perfect flowers, running for mayor, every promise blooms the second he says it) -> plants (instant blooms; bees never land on him) -> stake (his first job: bulldoze the park and Grandma's hives) -> your promise (save her bees: a bud on your hand) -> weird prep (all 10,000 bees in a shoebox) -> doubter (Grandma: 'a thousand flowers vs a bud') -> setback (99 % in the polls, your bud browning) -> big test (bees land on every real flower except Derek's) -> reversal: the rival's own habit (he PROMISES they're real: a real flower shoots out of his nose and rots on live TV) -> reveal (sweat, glue, 1,000 fake flowers slide off, 1,000 rotten ones underneath) -> callback (you can smell him from across the mall) -> loop: your one bud blooms
loop: Line 1: every promise you make grows a flower out of your skin. Last: your one little bud (Grandma's 'You've got a bud') finally blooms: the rule closes on you, kept.

voiceNotes.grandma: Lily (ElevenLabs premade): warm, velvety British woman, the closest premade to a fond, teasing grandma
voiceNotes.derek: Callum (ElevenLabs premade): husky trickster, a slick candidate with something to hide

facts: Fiction: no sources needed. One rule, said in line 1-2 and shown before it matters: every promise grows a flower out of the promiser's skin; kept = it blooms, broken = it rots and stinks.

Fallout of the same rule (not new rules): a promise that is already false rots the moment it is said (Derek's nose flower); bees land only on real flowers (planted in line 9, shown with a bee snubbing Derek).
Derek's 1,000 blooms are glued-on fakes hiding 1,000 rotten real ones; the clue is that his flowers bloom the second he promises (a real one only blooms once the promise is kept).
Numbers: 1,000 (Derek's flowers, the motif), 10,000 bees, 99 % in the polls: story numbers.

lines.narration: In this world, every promise you make grows a *flower* out of your skin.
lines.scene: Cold open, a sunny small-town square: a man on a bench takes his date's hands and says something; POP, a green bud shoots out of his elbow. Around them, everyone carries flowers growing out of arms, shoulders, heads: a mail carrier with daisies up both arms, a kid with one sprout on his knee.
lines.camera: MCU on the couple, the bud pops on 'flower', quick pull-out to the square full of flowered people
lines.gag: A bud pops out of a man's elbow the instant he says 'I promise'

lines.narration: Keep it, and it *blooms*.
lines.scene: Macro: the elbow bud unfurls into a big red flower, petals opening in a burst, pollen sparkles in the sun.
lines.camera: Macro push-in, the bloom opens on 'blooms'
lines.gag: The bud bursts into a bloom like a party popper

lines.narration: Break it, and it rots and *stinks*.
lines.scene: Same framing, match cut: the flower droops brown, petals fall, three flies circle it, green stink lines rise; a passing jogger gags and veers away.
lines.camera: Same macro (match cut), then a hard cut to the jogger's disgusted face
lines.gag: Flies circle the rotten flower and a jogger gags mid-stride

lines.narration: You see, Linda ran the marathon she promised: a sunflower on her *knee*.
lines.scene: Linda (headband, running vest with a race number) jogs past your fence, a giant sunflower blooming from her knee, bobbing with every stride, a finisher medal round her neck.
lines.camera: Tracking her jog in profile, the sunflower bobbing
lines.gag: The sunflower on her knee bounces like a bobblehead as she jogs

lines.narration: Dad's sink promise? Six years old. Dead tulip, on his *ear*.
lines.spoken: Dad's sink promise? SIX years old. Dead tulip, on his ear.
lines.scene: Kitchen: Dad reads the paper beside a sink with a bucket under a dripping tap; a shrivelled brown tulip hangs off his ear, a fly circling it. He waves the fly off without looking up.
lines.camera: MS on Dad and the bucket, quick push to the rotten tulip on 'ear'
lines.onScreenText: A sticky note on the tap: FIX ME
lines.gag: A bucket overflowing under the sink and a fly orbiting Dad's ear

lines.narration: And the guy who said "I'll call you"? You can smell him from across the *mall*.
lines.scene: A mall: far down the walkway a guy scrolling his phone, a brown rotten rose on his shoulder; a thick green stink cloud drifts the full length of the mall, shoppers fanning their noses, a dog fainting.
lines.camera: Long telephoto down the mall, the cloud rolling toward the lens on 'mall'
lines.gag: The stink cloud rolls the whole length of the mall; a dog faints

lines.narration: Then there's Derek: a thousand perfect flowers, like a walking wedding *cake*.
lines.spoken: Then there's Derek: a THOUSAND perfect flowers, like a walking wedding cake.
lines.scene: The town park: Derek steps out of a shiny campaign van, covered head to toe in perfect pink and white blooms, teeth gleaming, a 'DEREK FOR MAYOR' banner behind him. He spritzes himself with a perfume bottle.
lines.camera: Low angle tilt up Derek from his flowered shoes to his grin
lines.gag: Derek is so covered in flowers he looks like a three-tier wedding cake

lines.narration: He's running for mayor, promising free pizza, a water park, and no more *Mondays*.
lines.scene: Derek at a podium in the park, crowd cheering; each promise he shouts, a fresh perfect bloom appears on his sleeve. Inserts: a pizza, a waterslide, a calendar with Monday crossed out.
lines.camera: Hard cuts on each promise, MCU of Derek
lines.onScreenText: Calendar page with MONDAY crossed out
lines.gag: A calendar where Monday is torn out

lines.narration: And they bloom the *second* he says them.
lines.scene: Macro on Derek's sleeve: he says 'promise', and a flower is just THERE, fully open, no bud. Behind his back his other hand tucks a glue tube into his pocket (planted, easy to miss).
lines.camera: Macro on the sleeve, quick rack to his hidden hand
lines.gag: A bloom appears fully open with no bud, like a magic trick

lines.narration: Weirdly, bees never land on *him*.
lines.scene: A bee buzzes up to Derek's chest of flowers, sniffs one, recoils, and zigzags away gagging. Derek doesn't notice.
lines.camera: Follow the bee in close, it lands, sniffs, flies off toward the lens
lines.gag: A bee sniffs Derek's flower and flies off disgusted

lines.narration: But as mayor, he'll bulldoze Grandma's *beehives*.
lines.scene: Derek points his campaign plan at the park's corner: Grandma's little white beehives under an apple tree; a big yellow bulldozer sits on the plan board, ready.
lines.camera: Whip from Derek's pointing finger to the hives
lines.gag: The plan board shows the hives replaced by a parking lot

lines.narration: So you promise to save them, and a bud pops out of your *hand*.
lines.scene: At the hives: Grandma (beekeeper hat with veil pushed up, cardigan) looks up at you; you take her hands, and a tiny green bud pops out of the back of your hand.
lines.camera: Two-shot, then macro on your hand as the bud pops on 'hand'
lines.gag: Your bud is tiny next to Derek's thousand

lines.narration: You borrow all her bees. In a *shoebox*.
lines.spoken: You borrow all her bees. In a SHOEBOX.
lines.scene: Grandma's shed: you hold a sneaker shoebox, rubber bands round it, the lid bulging and buzzing; a few bees peek out of the air holes.
lines.camera: Push-in on the bulging, buzzing shoebox
lines.onScreenText: Sticker on the box: 10,000 BEES - DO NOT SHAKE
lines.gag: The shoebox lid hops up and down from 10,000 bees

lines.narration: "Sweetie, he's got a thousand flowers. You've got a *bud*."
lines.speaker: grandma
lines.scene: Grandma pats your hand and taps your tiny bud with one finger, a fond, doubtful look; over her shoulder through the window, Derek's flowered billboard.
lines.camera: MCU on Grandma, insert of her finger tapping the bud on 'bud'
lines.gag: She flicks your tiny bud and it wobbles

lines.narration: But by Thursday, Derek's at 99 percent, and your bud's turning *brown*.
lines.spoken: But by Thursday, Derek's at ninety-nine percent, and your bud's turning brown.
lines.scene: Night, Grandma's kitchen: the TV shows a poll bar, DEREK 99 %; you stare at your hand, the bud's edges going brown; a lone fly lands next to it. Blue night outside, warm lamp inside.
lines.camera: Over the TV to your face, then macro on the browning bud
lines.gag: A fly lands beside your bud like it's waiting

lines.narration: Friday's debate. You lift the *lid*.
lines.scene: Bright morning, the park: a debate stage, a crowd on folding chairs, news cameras. Derek beams at the podium in full bloom. You, front row, slowly lift the shoebox lid.
lines.camera: Wide of the stage, cut to you in the front row, macro on the lid lifting
lines.gag: A single bee climbs out first and looks around

lines.narration: Ten thousand bees pour out, onto every real *flower*.
lines.spoken: Ten thousand bees POUR out, onto every real flower.
lines.scene: A golden cloud of bees erupts from the box, sweeps over the crowd and settles on real blooms: Linda's knee sunflower, the bench guy's elbow flower, Grandma's roses. Nobody gets stung: people giggle.
lines.camera: Ride with the swarm over the crowd (object POV), sweeping toward the stage
lines.gag: Bees cover Linda's knee sunflower like a fuzzy blanket

lines.narration: Every flower... except *Derek's*.
lines.scene: The swarm hits the stage, splits around Derek like water round a rock, and leaves him standing alone in a ring of empty air. The crowd turns to look at him.
lines.camera: Wide on the stage as the swarm parts, then a slow push on Derek's frozen grin
lines.gag: The swarm parts around Derek like he's a rock in a river

lines.narration: "Pfft. Bees? I promise these flowers are *real*!"
lines.speaker: derek
lines.scene: Derek laughs too loudly into the microphone, slaps his flowered chest, sweat starting on his brow.
lines.camera: MCU on Derek, low angle
lines.gag: He slaps his chest and a fake petal falls off

lines.narration: Pop! A new flower shoots out of his *nose*.
lines.scene: POP: a real green stem shoots out of the tip of Derek's nose and opens a small flower. He goes cross-eyed looking at it.
lines.camera: Hard cut to a CU, crash zoom on 'nose'
lines.gag: Derek goes cross-eyed at the flower on his nose

lines.narration: And it rots. Right there. On live *TV*.
lines.scene: The nose flower wilts brown in seconds, petals drop, flies arrive; a news camera's red LIVE light; the crowd gasps and pinches noses.
lines.camera: Push on the rotting flower, cut to the news camera's LIVE light on 'TV'
lines.gag: The flower wilts like a time-lapse in two seconds flat

lines.narration: He sweats, so the glue melts, and his flowers slide off like wet *stickers*.
lines.scene: Sweat pours down Derek; his perfect flowers peel off in sheets, slide down his suit and pile at his feet; a glue tube falls out of his pocket.
lines.camera: Tilt down Derek as the flowers slide, following them to the pile
lines.gag: A thousand flowers peel off him in one sheet like a banana skin

lines.narration: Underneath? A thousand *rotten* ones.
lines.scene: Derek stands covered in brown rotten stumps, a fly cloud rising off him, green stink lines; the front row tips over backwards in their chairs.
lines.camera: Pull back fast to a wide as the stink wave hits the crowd
lines.gag: The whole front row falls backwards from the smell

lines.narration: Derek loses. You can smell him from across the *mall*.
lines.scene: The same mall telephoto as line 6: now Derek at the far end with a shopping bag, a stink cloud twice as big rolling the length of the mall; the 'I'll call you' guy next to him fans his own nose.
lines.camera: Mirror of the line 6 mall telephoto, the cloud rolling toward the lens
lines.onScreenText: Newspaper on a bench: DEREK LOSES
lines.gag: Even the 'I'll call you' guy holds his nose next to Derek

lines.narration: And your little bud finally *blooms*.
lines.scene: The park at the hives, golden light: Grandma beside you, bees back home; on your hand the bud bursts open into a big rust-orange flower, and a bee lands on it. Your smug, proud face, the hives blurred behind.
lines.camera: Macro on the bloom, rack to your face close-up on the last word
lines.gag: A bee lands on your flower, the first one that ever picked you
